headline: Failed House bill would have let employers offer voluntary after-hours training that does not count as paid work time.
what_it_does: The bill would have changed the Fair Labor Standards Act's definition of "hours worked." Voluntary training taken outside an employee's regular work hours would not count as hours worked, even if the employer offered it. This would apply only if employees who skip the training face no harm to their working conditions and if employees do no actual work for the employer during the training.

who_it_affects.group: Hourly workers covered by federal wage and overtime rules
who_it_affects.how: Time spent in voluntary, employer-offered training outside their regular hours would not have counted toward pay or overtime.
They could have offered optional after-hours training without having to pay for that time, as long as the bill's conditions were met.
